The measuring device is designed to measure the position of a first body relative to a second body. For this purpose, a scale band may be attached to the first body, while two marker detection sensors may be attached to the second body. The scale band includes a marker that can be detected by the marker detection sensors as the first and second bodies move relative to one another.

The marker is formed by a pattern of marker stripes. These marker stripes include transitions that are inclined at predetermined angles with respect to the transverse direction of the scale band. Each of the inclination angles is different from the others, thereby allowing the marker to provide distinguishable positional information. The scale band is further divided into a first trace and a second trace, which may be used in combination with the two marker detection sensors to detect and evaluate the marker pattern accurately.

A measuring device is provided for determining the position of a first body relative to a second body. The measuring device includes a scale band arranged on one of the bodies and a sensor arrangement arranged on the other body, so that movement between the two bodies can be detected by scanning the scale band. The scale band extends in a measuring direction and carries a marker pattern formed by a plurality of marker stripes. These marker stripes are arranged in at least two separate traces extending along the measuring direction.

Each trace includes stripe regions and stripe transitions. The stripe transitions are not all oriented in the same way; instead, they are formed with different inclination angles relative to the measuring direction or relative to a transverse direction of the scale band. In particular, the transitions in one trace may be inclined at a first angle, while the transitions in the other trace may be inclined at a second, different angle. As a result, the marker pattern produces a characteristic signal sequence when scanned by the sensor arrangement.

The sensor arrangement includes two marker detection sensors positioned so that each sensor scans one of the traces of the scale band. As the bodies move relative to one another, the sensors detect the passage of the marker stripes and the corresponding stripe transitions. Because the transitions in the two traces have different inclinations, the detected signals vary in a manner that depends on the exact relative position of the bodies. The combination of the signals from the two marker detection sensors therefore provides positional information that is more specific than would be obtained from a simple repetitive stripe pattern.

By arranging the stripe transitions at distinct inclination angles across the two traces, the marker pattern can encode unique position information along the measuring path. The measuring device can evaluate the sensor signals to determine the relative position of the first body with respect to the second body, and to distinguish between different positions that might otherwise produce similar sensor responses. This allows reliable and accurate detection of relative displacement.

The configuration is particularly useful in applications where two components move with respect to one another and their relative position must be monitored continuously or at defined points. The use of a scale band with patterned marker stripes and two corresponding marker detection sensors provides a robust and compact measuring system. Since the positional information is derived from the geometry of the marker pattern, especially from the differently inclined stripe transitions, the system can improve measurement reliability and reduce ambiguity in position detection.
outputs.L5:
A measuring device is an instrument used to determine the size, amount, weight, temperature, pressure, distance, or other properties of an object or environment. Measuring devices are important in everyday life, science, engineering, medicine, and industry because they help provide accurate and reliable information.

Common examples of measuring devices include rulers, thermometers, scales, measuring tapes, stopwatches, and pressure gauges. A ruler measures length, a thermometer measures temperature, and a scale measures weight or mass. More advanced measuring devices, such as digital calipers, laser distance meters, and electronic sensors, are used when high precision is required.

The main purpose of a measuring device is to make comparisons using standard units, such as meters, kilograms, seconds, or degrees Celsius. Accuracy is very important because even a small error can affect results, especially in scientific experiments or technical work. For this reason, many measuring devices must be checked and calibrated regularly.

Today, many measuring devices are digital, making them easier to read and often more precise than traditional tools. They can also store data, connect to computers, and provide quick results. Whether simple or advanced, a measuring device plays an essential role in helping people understand and control the world around them.
